title: Regression Cascade Escalation and Customer Guardrails
author: Maya Santos
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the observable triggers, triage steps, mitigation actions, and customer communications for simultaneous model-quality regressions and inference cost or token-spend spikes (a "regression cascade"). It is intended for Customer Success, First-Line Support (L1), SRE, and Runtime Engineering to rapidly protect customer SLAs while preserving throughput and minimizing rollback scope.

When to use this playbook:
- Any time a customer, tenant, or cohort exhibits a quality drop (synthetic-eval delta or customer complaint) that co-occurs with a >30% increase in per-request cost or per-token compute time for the same time window.
- Automated detection fires when both a quality metric and a cost/latency metric cross configured thresholds (see Detection and triggers).

Goals and guardrails:
- Protect customer-facing applications within 15–60 minutes for critical customers.
- Maintain availability SLO: 99.9% request success for dedicated tenants; 99.5% for hosted API customers.
- Limit blast radius: prefer per-tenant or per-route mitigations before global rollbacks.
- Preserve telemetry for postmortem and for QBR discussion.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Customer Success (owner): primary comms to customer, coordinate QBR follow-up and mitigations with engineering.
- L1 Support: initial alert acknowledgment, surface customer impact, apply documented mitigations (circuit-breakers, throttles, short-term rate-limits).
- Runtime/SRE (on-call): containment actions (fallback routing, model variant switch, capacity throttles).
- Runtime Engineering/Model Onboarding: root-cause investigation for model artifact or quantization regressions.
- Trust & Safety / Security (if sensitive data exposure suspected): immediate involvement.

Detection and triggers (signals):
- Quality signals (any of):
  - "quality_score_delta" (synthetic eval score) <= -4.0 points over baseline in last 30m.
  - Increase in customer-reported output variance or repeat-content ratio >2x.
  - Automated eval alert: personalisation-eval-failure rate >5% on golden prompts.
- Cost / performance signals (any of):
  - per-request GPU ms p95 increases by >40% vs baseline over 30m.
  - per-token compute cost (GPU-time tokens) > 1.3x baseline for the same model/sequence distribution.
  - Unexpected spike in per-tenant charges or throttling events.
- Composite trigger (requires 1 quality + 1 cost signal):
  - Composite_Regression_Cascade = true when both cross thresholds within same 30-minute window.

Immediate triage (0–15 minutes):
1) Acknowledge the alert and tag in incident channel: #cust-alerts/regression-cascade, post short summary and links to dashboards.
2) L1: confirm customer impact and severity using:
   - Query: SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE tenant_id = <T> AND last_30m AND (quality_score < baseline - 4 OR error IS TRUE);
   - Dashboard panels to check: "Tenant: Quality Heatmap", "Tenant: Per-request CPU/GPU ms", "Model: Canary eval pass rate".
3) If critical customer affected (enterprise plan, SLA-bound), escalate immediately to Runtime/SRE on-call and Customer Success (use the on-call rota).

Containment steps (15–60 minutes):
1) Apply per-tenant defensive throttling: reduce burst allowance to 30% for the tenant for 30 minutes. CLI example:
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/tenants/<T>/throttle -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"burst":0.3, "duration_minutes":30}'
2) Route affected traffic to fallback model variant (lower-latency or previously-known-good model):
   - Preferred order: model.fallback.stable -> model.fallback.quantized -> model.fallback-smaller.
   - API example to pin model:
     PATCH /v1/tenants/<T>/routes/<route_id>
     {"pinned_model": "gpt-open-4-fallback-v2"}
3) If regression accompanied by tokenization anomalies, enable prefix-caching bypass and drop aggressive auto-batching for the tenant to isolate KV-cache behavior.
4) Open a short-lived incident channel and attach traces, request ids, and representative failing outputs. Preserve at least 72 hours of request bodies for postmortem (encrypted at rest).

Mitigation and customer protection (60–240 minutes):
1) Apply model-level rollback if artifact/weight corruption is suspected. Rollback checklist:
   - Confirm candidate model SHA and compare checksums: sha256sum model-vX.tar.gz
   - Verify that the previous model variant (vX-1) had stable synthetic-eval metrics for the affected prompts.
   - Initiate canary rollback with 5% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor quality/cost deltas.
2) If cost spike is due to a serving configuration (batching/sequence-length kernel changes): revert to previous kernel selection policy via runtime config flags. Example flag toggles:
   - runtime.feature_flags.kernel_selector = "legacy"
   - runtime.batch.window_ms = 10
3) For customer-facing protection, offer temporary quota relief or a safety-mode model with guaranteed latency and cost caps (coordinate with Finance for credits).
4) Customer Comms: Customer Success drafts an initial status note (see templates below) and schedules an incident-specific sync if the customer requests.

Longer-term analysis and QBR integration (>24 hours):
- Collect and store: request traces, model SHAs, quantization config, kernel selections, and the sequence-length distribution during the incident window.
- Postmortem: standard 5-part RCA (timeline, impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, preventive actions). Owner: Runtime Engineering. Deliverable within 72 hours.
- QBR inclusion: define actions and metrics to present to the customer (quality regression delta, unblock timeline, and planned mitigations).

Escalation matrix (summary):
- L1 Support (first 15m) -> Runtime/SRE on-call (15–60m) -> Runtime Engineering & Model Onboarding (60–240m) -> Engineering leadership + Customer Success + Finance (if credits needed).

Service-level thresholds and decision points table:
- If composite trigger active AND tenant is SLA-bound -> immediate route + pin fallback + notify exec on-call.
- If rollback candidate fails to recover quality for canary -> escalate to full rollback approval within 3 hours.

Runbook configs and alert rules (examples):
- Alert: tenant_quality_drop_30m
  - expr: delta(quality_score_sum[30m]) / avg(quality_score_sum[7d]) < -0.05
  - for: 10m
  - labels: severity=high, domain=quality
- Alert: tenant_cost_spike_p95
  - expr: increase(per_request_gpu_ms_p95[30m]) / avg(per_request_gpu_ms_p95[7d]) > 0.4
  - for: 10m
- Composite alert rule (pseudo):
  - if tenant_quality_drop_30m && tenant_cost_spike_p95 then fire Composite_Regression_Cascade (route to #cust-alerts/regression-cascade).

Customer communication templates (use Customer Success to tailor):
- Initial short status (sent within 30–60m):
  - Subject: Brief update on observed model quality and cost impact
  - Body: We detected an unexpected drop in output quality coincident with elevated inference latency/cost affecting your tenant. We have applied short-term mitigations (pinned fallback model + throttles) and are actively investigating root cause. We will share a follow-up within 3 hours with next steps. Owner: Customer Success (contact: cs-lead@redwood.ai).
- Follow-up (post-containment):
  - Body: Containment measures and observed effect (metrics), planned rollback or mitigation, expected timeline for full resolution, and next QBR-level artifacts.

Post-incident checklist (deliverables):
1) 72-hr initial RCA draft with timeline and telemetry (Runtime Eng).
2) Customer-facing incident summary and compensation proposal where applicable (Customer Success + Finance).
3) Config and automation changes to prevent recurrence (Infrastructure PRs, Model onboarding checks).
4) Update onboarding docs and QBR materials to include new detection rules and sample prompts for customers to exercise.

Appendix: handy commands and queries
- Fetch recent failing requests for tenant <T> (example):
  - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $READONLY" "https://telemetry.redwood.ai/api/v1/requests?tenant=<T>&since=30m&filter=quality_score<{{baseline-4}}"
- Pin a route to a fallback model (example):
  - curl -X PATCH 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/<T>/routes/<route_id> 
    -d '{"pinned_model":"gpt-open-4-fallback-v2","reason":"regression-cascade containment"}'
- Example Prometheus alert fragment (YAML-like):
  - alert: Composite_Regression_Cascade
    expr: (tenant_quality_drop_30m == 1) and (tenant_cost_spike_p95 == 1)
    for: 10m
    labels: {severity: critical}
